name: Inti

domain_history.domain: central Inca state deity, sun; believed ancestor of the Inca ruling dynasty; the Sapa Inca held the title Intip churin, "Son of the Sun," establishing his sacred right to rule; imperial expansion incorporated conquered peoples' local deities into the solar pantheon with Inti at the apex as state legitimating ideology

notes: Chief temple: the Qoricancha ("Golden Enclosure") in Cusco, which also housed shrines to Mama Killa, Illapa (thunder), and Viracocha (Viracocha's shrine set apart, reflecting his distinct creator status). Sourced from convergent tertiary/encyclopedic references; a named specialist monograph (e.g. Brian S. Bauer, The Sacred Landscape of the Inca: The Cusco Ceque System, University of Texas Press, 1998) was recommended by the research agent for stronger citation but not directly retrieved in this research pass.
